issues.display_title: Issue #1024: fix(editor): autosave drops an edit made while a save is in flight
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Found while recording the #1018 demo (2026-09-15) on a scratch copy of Square One Mall V6 (Demo). Two Area colours were set a few seconds apart. After a reload the second one was gone, although the editor had already shown "Saved just now". This is not specific to #1018: any canvas edit made during a save is exposed.

What happens

On a large project one autosave takes 3–7 s. The dev log showed saveFloorplanAction at 3.1 s, 3.3 s and 7.0 s. An edit made while a save is in flight is marked saved when that save lands, and it is never sent:

  1. saveNow reads the store once, at its start: const store = useMapStore.getState() (src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx:92). It serialises that state object (buildPersistedState(store, …), :140), so the edit is not in the request.
  2. When the request returns, store.markSaved() (:148) sets hasUnsavedChanges: false unconditionally (src/store/mapStore/projectSlice.ts:75).
  3. The edit had scheduled the 2 s autosave timer (:170-182). That timer is cleared by the effect's re-run, because the flag is now false. The unmount flush (:163-168) requires hasUnsavedChanges too.

The store holds the edit and the server does not, while the topbar keeps saying "Saved …" (it shows that whenever lastSavedAt is set). A reload, a closed tab or opening the project on another device loses the edit.

Related risk in the same function: saveNow has no in-flight guard. If the timer does fire during a long save, two saves run at once, and the older snapshot can land last.

Evidence

  • Scratch copy (deleted since):
    • Room 57's colour was set before a save started; Room 30's colour was set during a 7.0 s save.
    • Engine state before the reload had both colours.
    • After the reload: Room 57 = #e11d48, Room 30 = no colour.
  • Dev server log: three saveFloorplanAction calls, the last one 7.0 s long, then the reload's GET /editor/…. No fourth save.

Scope

  • Mark saved only what was sent. Remember which state the save serialised. After it lands, clear hasUnsavedChanges only if the store still holds that state; otherwise keep the flag so the autosave schedules a follow-up.
  • One save at a time. No second saveNow while one is in flight; changes made meanwhile get one follow-up save.
  • Honest topbar. Show "Unsaved changes" / "Saving…" rather than "Saved …" while newer changes are unsent.
  • Out of scope: backend changes; collab conflict handling.

Acceptance criteria

  • An edit made while a save is in flight is persisted by a follow-up save with no further user action.
  • Two saves never run at the same time, and the last save sent carries the newest state.
  • Unit test (next to src/components/editor/__tests__/EditorTopbar.autosave.test.tsx) with a slow saveFloorplanAction mock: an edit during the save is in the next request, and hasUnsavedChanges stays true until it lands.
  • The topbar does not show "Saved …" while newer changes are unsent.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after check on a scratch copy of a large project (edit during a save, reload, edit still there).

RESULT

Fixed on feature/1024-autosave-inflight-edit: commit 442c477, PR #1026 → development (merge fe70bfc).

  • One request at a time (EditorTopbar.tsx): a call arriving mid-request is dropped (autosave — the follow-up covers its work) or queued (the Save button, the unmount flush). This also closes the second half of the bug, where a timer firing during a long save started a concurrent request whose older snapshot could land last.
  • Mark saved only what was sent: after a request lands, hasUnsavedChanges is cleared only if persistedStateChanged reports nothing moved while it was out; otherwise saveNow sends a follow-up — at once for a queued Save or flush, after the usual quiet period otherwise.
  • The Save button shares the queue (trigger "manual", still skipping the status PATCH as it always has).
  • Topbar: "Unsaved changes" outranks "Saved …" while edits are unsent.
  • Tests: EditorTopbar.autosave.test.tsx +4, each with a save that hangs until the test releases it — the edit during a request, no second request alongside, a Save click mid-request, and leaving the editor mid-request. Mutation checks 5/5 caught. Full suite 261 files green; lint and tsc clean.
  • Checked in the app (scratch copy of Square One Mall V6, ~3 s saves, .playwright-mcp/demo/1024/probe-inflight-edit.mjs): Area B coloured while Area A's request was out; after a reload both colours are there, and the dev log shows two strictly sequential save cycles, the second carrying B.
  • Note: the loss was timing-dependent — it needed the in-flight save to land before the pending edit's 2 s timer fired. A longer save hit the concurrent-request path instead. The unit tests pin both.

issues.display_title: Issue #1028: feat(editor): loading overlay with phase indicator while the project editor loads (#1017)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1028-loading-overlay.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #1017 ("Implement a Loading Spinner Whenever the Project Editor is Opened"). Answers from the PM are in this comment thread:

  1. No percentage — a phase indicator is enough.
  2. The overlay covers everything while loading.
  3. Wording: "Loading project…", "Loading floor plan…", "Preparing editor…".
  4. Applies to all scopes, not only the first open.
  5. Use the final brand mark with a pulse animation.

Reference asset (255×255, from #1017): images/image-63c01bf4-9a13-400d-a36d-31ff1966d85f.png

Current state (checked in code, development fe70bfc)

There is no loading state anywhere in the editor.

  • The flag already exists and is ignored. useWizardPersistence returns hydrated, true once getFloorplanAction(projectId) has resolved and hydratePersistedState has run (src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:50, :106-118). src/app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx:18 destructures it and uses it only for beginEditSession and the ?empty=1 seed — never to gate what is rendered.

  • So an empty project is rendered instead of a loading one. EditorCanvas derives floorsPresent from the store (EditorCanvas.tsx:33-39); while the store is still empty that is false, so EmptyProjectPlaceholder shows "No floors yet" with a live Add Floor button and a working .txt drop zone (EmptyProjectPlaceholder.tsx:23, :34-40). The panel shows "Untitled project" / "No location set" (EditorPanel.tsx:101, :106).

  • How long that lasts. From the stopwatch in the video attached to #1017 (Square One Mall V6 on production):

    t on screen
    ~4.3 s editor route opens — "Untitled project", "No floors yet"
    ~23.9 s project name arrives, still "No floors yet" with Add Floor and the drop zone
    ~87 s the floor plan finally renders

    So about 83 seconds of a project that looks empty and accepts input. Adding a floor or dropping a file in that window acts on a half-loaded project.

  • No progress signal to read. getFloorplanAction is a server action: one fetch, then res.json() (src/actions/projects.ts:268-276). No stream, no events — which is why the PM's answer to drop the percentage matters: phases are all the data we have.

  • No spinner primitive. src/components/ui/ has none, and public/ has no brand mark — EditorTopbar.tsx:308 renders the wordmark as text.

  • Later phases. A level or building switch runs engine.loadModel synchronously and then engine.setBackdrop (FloorplanEditor.tsx:585-586), and setBackdrop loads the image fire-and-forget with no ready callback (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:346-373). The engine itself reports readiness through engineReady (FloorplanEditor.tsx:120).

Scope

  • Overlay component covering the whole editor — topbar, panel, canvas and footer — so nothing underneath can be clicked while it is up. Brand mark with a pulse animation, one line of phase text below it, no number and no progress bar.

  • Brand mark asset. Add the icon from #1017 to public/. Ask the PM for an SVG first; fall back to the PNG if that is all there is.

  • Phases, in the order they occur:

    • "Loading project…" — from mount until getProject answers (project name, access, status).
    • "Loading floor plan…" — until hydrated is true, and for the floor-plan image of the level being opened or switched to.
    • "Preparing editor…" — until the engine has the level's model on the canvas and has painted once.

  • All scopes, where there is a real wait:

    • opening /editor/<id> directly or from the dashboard;
    • arriving from the wizard;
    • switching level or building, when a new floor-plan image has to load;
    • leaving preview back into the editor, if anything has to be rebuilt.

    Do not show the overlay where nothing is actually awaited — a flash for a load that is already warm is worse than no overlay. A short grace period before it appears is acceptable.

  • The empty-project placeholder must not appear while loading. It is the one state today that invites a destructive action on an unloaded project.

Out of scope

  • The load time itself. 83 seconds is a performance problem in its own right, filed separately; this task only makes the wait honest.
  • A real percentage, a progress bar, and any change to how the payload is fetched.
  • /preview/[projectId], /v/[key] and /embed/[key] — the PM's answer is about the editor.

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening a project shows the overlay from the first paint until the editor is usable; "No floors yet", "Untitled project" and "No location set" are never visible for a project that has floors.
  • While the overlay is up, no control underneath can be clicked or focused — in particular Add Floor and the .txt drop zone.
  • The phase text moves through "Loading project…" → "Loading floor plan…" → "Preparing editor…" and each one is on screen only while that phase is actually running.
  • A project that genuinely has no floors still reaches EmptyProjectPlaceholder once loading finishes.
  • Switching level or building shows the overlay while the new floor-plan image loads, and does not flash when the image is already cached.
  • The brand mark pulses; no percentage or progress bar anywhere.
  • Unit tests: the overlay is up while hydrated is false and gone after it flips; the phase text follows the phase; the placeholder does not render during loading.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.
  • Demo recorded on a scratch copy of a large project, showing the whole open with no empty-state flash.

Notes

engine.loadModel is synchronous, so a phase switched immediately before it will not paint — the overlay has to be on screen for a frame before the blocking work starts, or the user sees nothing change.

RESULT

Implemented and released.

  • src/store/useEditorLoadingStore.ts — holds what is still awaited (project fetch, floorplan blob, model build, floor image) and derives the phase, earliest wait first.
  • src/components/editor/EditorLoadingOverlay.tsx — covers the whole editor, chrome included; brand mark with a pulse, one line of phase text, no percentage, 150 ms grace so a cached floor image never makes it blink.
  • public/brand-mark.png — the asset from #1017 (PNG; an SVG can replace it later).
  • src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts — sets the flags, and announces the build phase through flushSync plus a paint, because hydrating the blob is synchronous and would otherwise never let that phase reach the screen.
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/{context,model-sync}.ts — a new optional backdrop callback so the floor image, the one awaited part of a level switch, is reported.
  • src/components/editor/{EditorCanvas,FloorplanEditor}.tsx, src/app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx — mount the overlay, report the canvas, and keep the empty-project card out of the way until the load finishes.

Tests: EditorLoadingOverlay (7), EditorCanvas.loading (2), both mutation-checked. pnpm test 263 files / 2425 passed, lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean.

GPU probe on a scratch copy of Square One Mall V6: 72 s of loading covered end to end, empty card never shown. Holding the file endpoint for 6 s moves the phase to "Loading floor plan…" and the overlay waits for the image.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1028/video-1028-loading-overlay.mp4 (23 s, 1920x1080 60 fps). The "before" is the video attached to #1017.

Note: the overlay waits out the slower of the two fetches — getProject carries canvas_data, so it races getFloorplanAction and either can be the long pole. The 83-second open itself is a separate performance problem, untouched here.

Commit: 0ca890a · PR #1029 → development (a8d9d4c) · released PR #1030 → main (858be78)

issues.display_title: Issue #1031: perf(editor): opening a large project takes over a minute — measure it, then cut it (#1017)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1031-one-request.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #1017. The loading overlay (#1028) covers the wait; it does not shorten it. This task is the wait itself.

What is measured

Two independent runs on Square One Mall V6, from the editor URL to a usable editor:

run what it showed
PM's video on #1017 (production) project name at ~23.9 s, floor plan rendered at ~87 s
My probe 2026-09-16 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1028/probe-loading-phases.mjs, local FE against the production API, scratch copy) overlay up 1.9 s → 72.0 s

Interesting detail from the probe: the long pole swapped. In the PM's run the project metadata answered first and the floorplan blob was late; in mine the blob came back first and getProject was the one that took 67 s. Both requests are slow, and either can be the one that decides when the editor opens.

First lead, checked in code (development a8d9d4c)

The editor downloads the project's geometry twice, on every open:

  • getProject → GET /v1/projects/:id (src/actions/projects.ts:128-142). The row carries canvas_data and generated_twin (:42-43), i.e. the whole floorplan JSON, and useWizardPersistence hydrates the store from it (:255-275).
  • getFloorplanAction → GET /v1/floorplan/:id (src/actions/projects.ts:268-276). The persisted blob carries canvasData, floorConfigs, informationRecords, eventRecords and the rest of PERSISTED_FIELDS (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:94-99), and hydratePersistedState writes those to the store as well.

Both are fired from the same hook on mount, in parallel, and both hydrate — the second one to land overwrites, guarded only by hasUnsavedChanges. So the same geometry crosses the wire twice, is JSON-parsed twice, and passes through two Next server actions (which re-serialize it into the RSC stream on the way back).

That is a lead, not a conclusion. The measurement comes first.

Scope

  1. Measure where the time goes, per open, on a scratch copy of a large project:
    • the API's own time for /v1/projects/:id and /v1/floorplan/:id (curl against the API directly, so the server action and RSC overhead are excluded);
    • the payload size of each;
    • the server action's added time on top of the API call;
    • client-side parse and hydrate time, and the engine's model build.
  2. Then act on what dominates. Likely candidates, in the order they are worth trying:
    • stop fetching the geometry twice — one load path for the editor, with the other request reduced to the fields it alone provides (name, status, access, location);
    • a lighter project endpoint or a field selector, if the row has to stay as it is (backend change — flag before starting, and file it on the API repo's board, Project #112);
    • compression on the two responses, if they are being served uncompressed;
    • keep the first paint from waiting on anything it does not need.
  3. Re-measure and report the before/after on the same project.

Out of scope

  • The loading overlay itself (#1028), which is shipped.
  • Changing what a project stores, or any migration of existing rows.
  • Editing the Go API contract without flagging it first.

Acceptance criteria

  • A written breakdown of the open, by stage, with numbers from a scratch copy of a large project (Square One Mall V6 or comparable): API time and payload size per request, server-action overhead, parse/hydrate, model build.
  • The geometry is not fetched twice per open, or there is a written reason why it still has to be.
  • Measured improvement on the same project, reported before/after with the same method.
  • Any backend need is filed separately on Project #112 and linked here, not merged into this task.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; no change to what is persisted.

Notes

  • The dev frontend talks to the production API, so measure on a scratch copy — never on a customer project.
  • .playwright-mcp/demo/1028/probe-loading-phases.mjs already reports the phase timeline per painted frame and is the obvious starting point for the before/after.

RESULT

The measurement

Five opens of the same project (scratch copy of Square One Mall V6), timings from Next's own server-action log, which is essentially the API call:

call endpoint duration
getFloorplanAction GET /v1/floorplan/:id 8.0 s, 16.5 s, 28.3 s, 31.6 s, 52.7 s
getProject GET /v1/projects/:id 0.345, 0.378, 0.388, 0.395, 0.398 s

One endpoint is the whole wait, and it varies 6x on identical input. Payload ~2.33 MB of JSON, ~677 kB on the wire. A CPU profile across a 65 s open: 44 % idle, 22 % unattributed browser time, the rest spread across canvas fill and three.js geometry — nothing on the client that would explain a minute.

The lead written into this task was wrong. The geometry is not fetched twice: GET /v1/projects/:id answered with 643 bytes, so its canvas_data is not populated for this project. Two other things were, and both are fixed.

Fixed (PR #1036, released in PR #1037)

  • Two serialized round trips became one. Next runs server actions one at a time: the project row was not sent until the floorplan blob had been consumed, and by then the browser was busy building the model, so a 0.4 s call landed 20-30 s late and held the editor shut for all of it. getEditorBootstrapAction asks for both and runs the API calls side by side on the server. The wizard keeps its own getProject — it has no blob to fetch.
  • The floor image is fetched once. loadModel clears the backdrop and the host re-applies it, so every store-side edit — area info, a pin drag, a bulk panorama import — downloaded the same image again. The engine now keeps the decoded image and re-applies it.

Tests: useWizardPersistence.bootstrap (2), backdrop-dedupe (4). pnpm test 265 files / 2431 passed, lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1031/video-1031-one-request.mp4 — the same project opened against development and against the branch, with a panel listing every request:

before   at 1.6s  floorplan blob            59 kB   1.5s
         at 3.0s  project row                1 kB   0.7s   <- only after the blob is back
         at 4.0s  floor image              148 kB   2.8s

after    at 1.4s  floorplan + project row   60 kB   2.1s
         at 4.9s  floor image              148 kB   1.2s

Not delivered, and why

A credible before/after wall clock. The API swings 8-53 s for the same request, which swamps anything the frontend does. What is deterministic, and what the tests pin, is the request count. Real open-time numbers only become meaningful once the API side lands: Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#179 (Project #112, To do), which carries the table above.

Noted while measuring, not addressed

The editor sends an updateProject carrying the whole generatedTwin on every open — a write on a read path, present on development too. Being looked at separately.

Commit: 0f6ba0c · PR #1036 -> development (70f29cd) · released PR #1037 -> main (01da28b)

issues.display_title: Issue #1035: feat(editor): colour for Room and Hallway room types (#1032)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1035-room-hallway-color.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #1032. A room typed Room or Hallway has no colour control — the toolbar only offers Height and Type. Colour is currently reachable for a Closed room (#1016) and for a standalone Area (#1018), and nothing else.

What exists today

The gate is one condition in the selection toolbar:

src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/SelectionToolbars.tsx:338
{selArea?.type === "closed" && (() => { ... Color + Opacity + Logo ... })()}

Most of the machinery underneath is already type-agnostic:

  • setAreaColor (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts:182) writes color onto areaMeta for any room index — it never looks at the type.
  • The map's paint expressions (src/lib/map/layer-definitions.ts:29) coalesce onto a feature's areaColor / areaLineColor, so any feature carrying those keys is painted.
  • A Room already stores a colour. src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:1336 says so outright: "A Room's own leftover color (kept for switching back to Closed) paints nothing."

So this is mostly un-gating the control and letting the colour reach the floor slab.

Decisions (answered by PM on #1032)

  1. Floor fill only. A Room or Hallway does not tint its bounding walls. That behaviour stays exclusive to Closed rooms (PRD R9), whose walls belong to one room; a Room shares its walls with its neighbours and tinting them would bleed the colour next door.
  2. Colour only. No opacity slider for Room/Hallway in this task — the stepped opacity from #1019 stays a Closed-room control.
  3. A small reset button next to the picker, clearing the colour back to the default floor slab. <input type="color"> cannot be empty, so without it a room can never go back to plain cream once it has been coloured.
  4. The colour survives a type switch. Converting Closed → Room keeps the colour the user picked and now paints with it. Reset (3) is the way out.

Scope

  1. Toolbar (SelectionToolbars.tsx) — a Colour control plus a reset button for room / hallway (and for an untyped room, which reads as "Room"). Leave the Closed block (Colour + Opacity + Logo) as it is.
  2. Clearing a colour — setAreaColor currently only writes a string. It needs to be able to remove the key so "no colour" is representable again.
  3. Editor 2D (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:105) — this loop does two jobs with one map: it fills the room and collects the bounding walls to tint. Per (1) the wall tint must stay Closed-only, so the two have to be split. draw.ts already reads areaMeta by room index (:113), so the type is available without a new context field.
  4. Editor 3D pane (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/scene3d.ts:101) — the floor colour already reads ctx.areaColors, so it follows for free. But :108 applies a stored opacity whenever a room has a colour; that must be gated to Closed, or a room converted from Closed would keep a leftover 40 % floor.
  5. Map / visitor map / embed (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:1338) — emit areaColor + areaLineColor for a coloured Room/Hallway, following the standalone-Area branch. Do not emit areaOpacity for them.
  6. Feeding the engine (closedRoomColors in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/closedRoom.ts:413, called from src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:652) — it filters to type === "closed"; it needs to carry coloured Rooms and Hallways too.

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting a room typed Room or Hallway shows a colour picker and a reset button in the toolbar.
  • Picking a colour fills that room's floor in the editor 2D canvas, the editor 3D pane, the Map tab, and the visitor map / embed.
  • The room's walls keep their default paint — no colour on a Room's or Hallway's bounding walls anywhere.
  • Reset returns the room to the default floor slab on every one of those surfaces.
  • One colour-picker drag is one undo step, and a picker opened and dismissed with Esc writes nothing — the existing beginAreaColorEdit / commitAreaColorEdit gesture rules.
  • Converting Closed → Room keeps the colour and paints with it; the leftover Closed opacity does not apply to the Room.
  • No opacity control appears for Room or Hallway.
  • Open (open-to-below) is unchanged — it has no floor slab to colour.
  • The colour survives save + reload.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit all green.

RESULT

Fix

8a60607 feat(editor): floor colour for Room and Hallway room types — PR #1039

The colour picker was gated to type === "closed" in the selection toolbar, so a Room or a Hallway had Height and Type and nothing else. It now has Color and a reset button, for room, hallway and an untyped room alike.

Per the PM's answers on #1032:

  • Floor only. A Closed room tints its bounding walls (PRD R9) because it renders as one solid mass and owns them; a Room shares its walls with its neighbours, so a tint would bleed next door. draw.ts now fills every coloured room but collects bounding walls only for a Closed one, and geojson-utils emits areaColor + areaLineColor for a Room/Hallway and no areaColorDark.
  • Colour only. No opacity slider; scene3d gates the stored opacity to Closed, so a room converted out of Closed does not keep a see-through floor.
  • Reset clears back to the default slab — a colour input can never be empty.
  • The colour survives a type switch. Converting Closed → Room paints with the colour the record was already keeping.

open-to-below is unchanged: it has no floor slab to paint. No new dependency, no Go API change.

closedRoomColors became roomFillColors; setAreaColor takes string | null.

One trap: reset writes an explicit color: null rather than deleting the key. metaOf (bridge.ts:294) reads an ABSENT key as "the engine has nothing to say, keep what the store had" and only an explicit null as "cleared" — a delete passes an in-memory test and then silently un-does itself on the next save, because the stored area still carries the old colour.

Verification

pnpm test 265 files / 2,448 passed, pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean. 14 new tests in room-color.test.ts, SelectionToolbars.roomColor.test.tsx, closedRoom.test.ts and geojson-area-color.test.ts, including a modelToLevel check that the reset is not undone by the save.

GPU Chrome on a scratch copy, driven through the real toolbar:

before Room coloured Hallway → Closed → back to Room
areas carrying areaColor 0 1 1 (areaType: hallway) 1 1 (areaType: room)
walls in our colour 0 0 0 11 0
walls tinted at all 18 18 18 27 18
areaOpacity — absent absent — absent
  • The colour survives save + reload; so does the reset.
  • 2D canvas and the editor's 3D pane: .playwright-mcp/screenshot/1035-2d-before.png vs -after.png.
  • Probes: .playwright-mcp/demo/1035/probe-room-color.mjs, probe-types.mjs.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1035/video-1035-room-hallway-color.mp4 (64 s, 1920x1080, 60 fps). Full take: -raw.mp4.

Not verified live

The visitor map /v/<key> and the embed were not opened directly. They share canvasDataToGeoJson with the Map tab and the unit tests cover both its flat and 3D modes, but the scratch copy is a draft, so there was no published key to load.

issues.display_title: Issue #1038: fix(editor): opening a project finishes the wizard again — a write, a deleted draft and a phantom funnel event on every open
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Found 2026-09-16 while measuring #1031: every single editor open sends a write, with no edit made.

└─ ƒ updateProject("<id>", {"generatedTwin":"…","isComplete":true,"status":"scanned"}) in 1022ms

Why it happens

src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts subscribes to the store and treats "the twin just appeared" as "the wizard just finished":

// AI scan complete (generatedTwin newly set): save twin + mark scanned.
if (!prev.generatedTwin && state.generatedTwin && state.projectId) {
  completeWizard(state.projectId, { generatedTwin: …, status: "scanned" }, { exit: "generated", … });
  wizardComplete.current = true;
}

The editor mounts this same hook. The restore effect calls reset() on mount, so prev.generatedTwin is null, and hydrating the project then sets it — the exact transition above. state.projectId is set in both contexts (setProjectId and setWizardProjectId both write it), so nothing else stops it.

The sibling reporter in the same effect already guards for this: reportStep opens with if (projectId) return;, on the hook's own argument, with a comment explaining that the editor mounts this hook and hydratePersistedState writes wizard state on every open. The twin branch never got the same guard.

What it costs (src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts)

  1. A write on a read path. The whole generatedTwin is PATCHed to the API on every open — to the same API whose slowness is the subject of #1031 and Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#179.
  2. It deletes the wizard's draft. localStorage.removeItem(storageKey()) drops the unkeyed wizard blob. Someone with a half-finished wizard who opens an existing project loses that draft.
  3. It reports a wizard completion that did not happen. trackEvent("wizard_completed", { exit: "generated" }) fires once per editor page load, into the funnel #698 exists to keep clean. Every editor open currently counts as a finished wizard.

Checked and NOT a problem

status: "scanned" is sent unguarded, while the editor's own save path deliberately refuses to downgrade a published project (EditorTopbar.tsx:124). It looked like opening a published project would unpublish it.
